Very fun little game. There's about 3 hours of content if you play through every mode and take your time exploring the levels. The guns feel powerful, and are very fun to use. The animations are overall great too, especially the reloads, which had me laughing the first time I saw them. Enemies telegraph their attacks well, and respond nicely to getting shot. The gore and gibs are also stellar. It's not a particularly hard game, even on the highest difficulty. Headshots deal extra damage, and combined with your absurd rate of fire it becomes pretty simple to completely plow through hordes of enemies without stopping. I didn't even really have to use the time-stop mechanics, despite it being a really cool feature. The level design is way better than you'd expect for a $5 indie boomer shooter, with a few of the later levels especially being honestly very well done. Ammo pickups are plentiful, but I still found myself scavenging for health at times, which is exactly the balance I enjoy. Bosses are alright, but can be cheesed pretty hard with the parry mechanic. The game needs a few little polishes here and there, like smoother transitions between gameplay and cutscenes (I accidentally skipped most of them my first time playing, since it gives you little warning one's about to start) or some more sound cues for boss attacks. The music is also kinda wonky, and doesn't loop properly on some levels. Some of the items you get for killing bosses are also implemented kinda weird. Instead of getting to control when you want to fly, for example, it just starts you flying at the beginning of every level, and when that wears off it's gone until the next level starts. A bit of a weird choice. It's also not really a roguelike at all, despite how it advertises itself. Nothing is randomly generated, and the upgrades you acquire upon killing bosses are permanent once you select them. You are also not punished for dying at any point, which is kinda a pro or a con depending on how you're handling the game. That being said, these are all minor gripes. The gameplay is good, the level design is good, and that's all you really need in a boomer shooter anyway. Overall a very good game which left me wishing there was more. It's extremely charming, and I enjoyed it enough to even show it off to some friends while I was playing it. Definitely worth the time I spent with it, and an easy recommend. If more content gets added, I will absolutely be revisiting the title.

Eh. I love the modelling and the nice looking design for the levels, but that's about it. Could be done a lot better with the right game design in mind. Lots of Cute Doom that sparkled my eyes, but overall for gameplay, it didn't really shine much of a light. I do like the way the architecture overall was done, albeit only a few details were eye catching. Quite bland enemies overall for a GZDoom game, specially for a Doom clone. The bosses were nothing unique and too easy overall, couldn't get to fug around with their attack patterns/bullet patterns at all because they died too fast. The fact you have to actively jump to reach some areas (and are expected to to even progress), with it being a Doom clone, feels absurdly just wrong too. Verticality as a mechanic is hard to pull with a base game that on its own is not made with that in mind, and it felt horrible to do anything vertical because of the high speed and slippery doom floor. Too focused on the characters being cute I'd say. But I dig it somewhat. Could be great if the gameplay overall was the main focus before mapping and design. Also I have 0 clue why it's called Roguelite if it has no aspects of Rogue. The upgrades carrying over to a new save (ng+) rather than dying is something completely different from the concept of rogue, and not even a roguelite characteristic on its own.

Not too keen on this one. A lot of my criticisms about the previous game still hold true, and in some ways, I think this game is actually a step back. Not to mention, this game is COMICALLY easy. In a little under an hour and a half, I beat normal and hard mode, and I don't care to play the game through a third time on one hit mode. Firstly, this game isn't even a roguelite. Not sure why that was put in the title. The only 'roguelite' element is a persistent upgrade system. I guess in that sense, Dark Souls is a roguelite because you get to do new game+ with your levels, too. Ignoring false advertising, the game is so-so. Like I said about the first game, I could see this being a charming WAD uploaded for free somewhere, but the fact that it's so short, doesn't provide really anything new from a gameplay perspective, and doesn't even have its own soundtrack really makes me disappointed. I'm not petty enough to refund the game despite clearing it so fast, but it really does feel like a shoddy project thrown together with little care or just as a meme. I was willing to be lenient with the first game, but a second entry doing the exact same thing says a lot about what's going on here. On my run through normal mode, I didn't even realize there were cutscenes after killing bosses. I only noticed because on hard mode, I saw like 3 frames of the first one. I'm assuming if you click even ONCE after killing the boss it somehow skips the cutscene. From what I was able to piece together (by conservatively shooting the bosses as to not accidentally skip) The story is largely nonsensical and a joke. This isn't inherently a bad thing, but mixed with everything else going on here, it leaves kind of a bad taste in my mouth. In short, if you don't mind spending $5 on a mediocre, silly GZDoom WAD, go for it. Otherwise, skip.
